newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil vote favored Cardoso's party - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Brazil vote favored Cardoso's party - Salomon.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's party fared well in last week's municipal voting although its candidate was badly beaten in the Sao Paulo mayor's race, Salomon Brothers Inc said in a report.
The investment bank, citing results from 26 state capitals, said that Cardoso's Social Democratic party (PSDB) won two state capitals and made it into mid-November second rounds in six others.
"The PSDB could conceivably emerge as the party with the strongest gains following the vote on November 15," it said.
"It appears set to triple the number of mayoralties under its control to about 900 given likely endorsements from other parties in the second round of voting."
Some 100 million Brazilians flocked to the polls last Thursday to elect mayors and councilmen in 5,500 cities and towns in Latin America's first-ever computerized vote.
Salomon Brothers downplayed the drubbing of PSDB candidate Jose Serra, the president's right-hand man, in the Sao Paulo mayor's race.
It said the PSDB is unlikely to back Celso Pitta of the Brazilian Progressive Party (PPB), who is expected to win a second-round victory in the Sao Paulo race.

Pitta's mentor and likely presidential hopeful Paulo Maluf, is expected to be emboldened and oppose Cardoso's bid to have Congress amend the constitution to allow him to run for an unprecedented second term.
Salomon also said the elections reveal the waning power of the Democratic Movement Party (PMDB), which is likely to register only a small gain in mayoralties.
A Cardoso cabinet reshuffle expected later this year or early in 1997 will seek to exploit rifts with the PPB over Maluf's opposition to re-election and reduce the influence of the PMDB, it added.
